newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares not for faint-hearted -- brokers.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares not for faint-hearted -- brokers.

text.p: The Turkish stock market has entered a period of extreme volatility driven by a political crisis which could translate into high-risk trading, brokers say.

Shares rose nearly five percent to a record 1,794 on the IMKB National-100 index in morning trading on Friday on growing hopes that a planned secularist coalition government may win a confidence vote in parliament.

The market, which jumped over 50 percent at the start of the year on hopes for privatisation, has recently been dominated by a political conflict which culminated last week in the resignation of Islamist prime minister Necmettin Erbakan.

"There are going to be incredible price movements in this period. Both the risks and the profits are high. The faint-hearted should steer clear of the stock market," said Mustafa Yilmaz, head of his own brokerage.

A week ago President Suleyman Demirel asked free-marketeer Mesut Yilmaz to form a government, fuelling expectations in the financial community of a broad-based government capable of pushing through economic reform.
"I see the current period as one of high risk and high profit," said Hayri Fevzioglu, deputy manager of Cagdas Securities.

Conservative Yilmaz is two votes short of the simple majority needed in parliament to win a confidence vote with the support of two left-wing parties and a right-wing group which broke away from the DYP.
Uncertainty over his chances was a cause of impatience among shares traders.
"The stock market wants to see a result," said Bihlun Tamayligil, deputy manager of Deha Securities.
"The bourse wants answers to questions -- what government will win a confidence vote? what will happen to economic and political plans and what will happen after an election?" Tamayligil said.
But Bayindir Securities general manager Semih Cetin forecast strong gains if there is more support from within the DYP for a government under Yilmaz.
"The DYP's stance is vital. If it supports the government it will have a positive impact on the market. This could lift the index to the 2,000 point level," Cetin said.

True Path leader Tansu Ciller, allied with the Islamists of outgoing prime minister Erbakan, has refused to discuss a coalition accord with Yilmaz. Consequently he will rely on more defections from her party to win a confidence vote within the next two weeks, brokers said.
